question: A 70-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination of diffuse exertional chest pain which he has successfully been treating with sublingual nitroglycerin for the past year. The patient has been taking lisinopril daily for essential hypertension. His pulse is 75/min and regular, and blood pressure is 155/90 mm Hg. Cardiac and pulmonary examination show no abnormalities; there is no peripheral edema. A decrease of which of the following is the most likely explanation for the improvement of this patient's chest pain?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) -> decreased afterload -> decreased myocardial oxygen demand -> improved chest pain -> 80%
CHAIN: Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor) -> decreased peripheral arterial resistance -> decreased cardiac workload -> improved chest pain -> 85%
enhanced_information: The improvement of the patient's chest pain is most likely due to the decrease in peripheral arterial resistance caused by lisinopril, leading to a reduction in cardiac workload and myocardial oxygen demand. This aligns with the consensus that decreased afterload and peripheral arterial resistance can improve chest pain in patients with hypertension.
